table.title: [val] Co-bottleneck · Framework trade-offs
table.md:
| Option | Strengths | Weaknesses | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Server rendering | Fast first paint, good for SEO, and simple caching at the CDN edge for anonymous pages. | Every interaction needs a round trip unless you add client code, and personalised pages are hard to cache. | Default |
| Static export | Cheapest to host and trivially scalable; pages survive backend outages. | Content updates need a rebuild, which gets slow once you have tens of thousands of pages. | Docs |
| Client SPA | Rich interactions and offline support once loaded. | Slow first load on mid-range phones, and search engines may index an empty shell. | Avoid |

understanding.purpose: Compare rendering frameworks by their strengths, weaknesses, and overall verdict.
understanding.reading: Readers scan the option names, compare the paired trade-offs across each row, and use the verdict for a quick assessment.
groups: Strengths and Weaknesses are parallel descriptions and should have comparable room for reading and comparison.
Option and Verdict frame each row with its identity and assessment.
may_wrap: Strengths and Weaknesses can wrap naturally at word boundaries; their longer descriptions will largely determine row height.

preferred.name: r3B
preferred.note: Split the descriptive space between r2A and r2B, giving Strengths a little more room while preserving a modest advantage for the longer Weaknesses content.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Take 10px from Verdict and give it to Strengths. This keeps option names and verdicts intact while giving the paired descriptions more balanced measures.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Keep the framing columns compact and give Strengths slightly more room than Weaknesses. Test whether its wrapping improves without making the weakness text noticeably less readable.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Give Weaknesses extra room while retaining 20px more for Strengths than r0C. Test a moderate version of the wider-weaknesses approach.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Test a midpoint between r1A and r1C, giving Weaknesses more room while trying to keep the first strength to three lines.

acceptable.name: r2B
acceptable.note: Reduce Verdict to its 73px minimum for the stated content and give those 5px to Strengths, preserving r1A’s weakness width.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Keep r1C’s wider Weaknesses column while reclaiming 5px from Verdict to improve the first strength’s wrap.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Move 5px from Verdict to Strengths while retaining r2A's Weaknesses width. This tests whether Strengths gains a more comfortable measure without sacrificing the clearer weakness wrapping.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The option column has only 74px of text width, forcing the two-word option labels to wrap and weakening the scan down the left edge, while giving more space to strengths than the longer weaknesses.
bad.why: The option column has only 74px of text width, forcing the two-word option labels to wrap and weakening the scan down the left edge, while giving more space to strengths than the longer weaknesses.

rationale: r3B keeps option names and verdicts on one line while giving the two substantive comparison columns most of the width. Weaknesses gets slightly more room, reflecting its longer content; the resulting line breaks are reasonably balanced across the three rows. The first row still has a four-line weakness, but that is shared by all the candidates.

general: Give columns space according to their content and role in comparison, rather than making them equal by default.
Keep labels and short decision cues easy to scan, while allowing prose to wrap at natural word boundaries.
specific: The weaknesses are longer than the strengths, so a modestly wider weaknesses column is useful.
The 73px verdict column fits its header and values, leaving more room for the comparison text.

tradeoffs: A wider strengths column, as in r1B, improves some line breaks there; a wider weaknesses column, as in r2C, gives the longer prose more room but makes the first strength four lines.
uncertain: The ranges are visual estimates, not verified breakpoints. They describe small adjustments with the other columns rebalanced proportionally within the 719px total; exact line breaks may change within them.

critique.good: Option names and verdicts stay on one line. The two trade-off columns are reasonably balanced, and each row is easy to follow across.
critique.problems: The first weakness sets a four-line row while its strength occupies three lines. Verdict has a little more room than its short values need.
critique.cause: The 260px Weaknesses column wraps the longest description to four lines; the 88px Verdict column leaves some space that could be used by the descriptions.

critique.good: The wider Strengths column gives its descriptions a comfortable measure, and verdicts remain intact.
critique.problems: Server rendering wraps to two lines, making the option labels less consistent and harder to scan. The first weakness still takes four lines.
critique.cause: The 110px Option column provides only 89px of text space, less than the 115px needed for the longest option name. Weaknesses has 255px.

critique.good: All option names and verdicts remain on one line. The wider Weaknesses column gives its longer descriptions room to read.
critique.problems: Strengths looks noticeably compressed beside Weaknesses. Its first description takes four lines, so the wider Weaknesses column does not reduce the first row's height; the last strength also wraps more than in the other designs.
critique.cause: The 205px Strengths column is narrow relative to the 300px Weaknesses column.

critique.good: The option names and verdicts remain intact, and the paired descriptions have a balanced visual weight. Each row is easy to follow across the table.
critique.problems: The first weakness takes four lines, leaving extra space beneath its three-line strength. The weakness column also determines the height of the last row.
critique.cause: At 260px, Weaknesses does not have quite enough room to reduce those descriptions to three and two lines respectively.

critique.good: The wider Strengths column gives the first description a comfortable three-line setting. Names, verdicts, and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: The narrower Weaknesses column still takes four lines in the first row and three in the last, so the extra strength width does not improve the table’s overall rhythm.
critique.cause: Moving 10px from Weaknesses to Strengths favors a column that was already shorter in most rows.

critique.good: The wider Weaknesses column gives the longer descriptions a more natural measure, and the last row’s weakness reads more smoothly.
critique.problems: The first strength now wraps to four lines, ending with the isolated word “pages.” The trade-off columns also look less balanced.
critique.cause: Reducing Strengths to 225px makes it too narrow for the first description, while the added width in Weaknesses does not reduce the first row’s height.

critique.good: The option names and verdicts stay on one line, and the trade-off columns are easy to compare across each row. The wider Weaknesses column accommodates its longer descriptions.
critique.problems: The first weakness occupies four lines, leaving a line of empty space beneath the corresponding strength. The Verdict column has slightly more room than its short entries need.
critique.cause: Weaknesses has 270px, while Verdict has 78px; some of the latter could be reassigned to the descriptive columns.

critique.good: The framing columns are compact, and the wider Strengths column gives the descriptions comfortable lines. All names, verdicts, and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: Weaknesses feels more constrained relative to its longer content. Its first entry still occupies four lines, and the Static export weakness wraps more heavily than in r2A.
critique.cause: Strengths receives 250px at the expense of Weaknesses, which receives 260px.

critique.good: The additional width in Weaknesses gives its longer descriptions a more relaxed measure, particularly in the Client SPA row. Names and verdicts remain intact.
critique.problems: The first Strengths entry wraps to four lines, leaving a short final line and making that column feel pinched beside Weaknesses.
critique.cause: Strengths is reduced to 230px while Weaknesses expands to 280px.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r3B.why: Option names and verdicts stay on one line, and the two descriptive columns have balanced widths. The longer weakness in the first row wraps to four lines.

r1A.why: Option names and verdicts remain intact, while the descriptive columns are well balanced. The first weakness takes four lines, leaving some space beside it.

r1B.why: The option names and verdicts scan cleanly, and both descriptive columns have comfortable widths. The first weakness wraps to four lines.

contrast.why: The descriptive columns have ample room, but two option names wrap, making the labels harder to scan down the first column.

ref_auto.why: The wider weaknesses column keeps the longest descriptions to three lines, producing a compact, even rhythm. Two option names wrap, though they remain readable.

ref_equal.why: Option and verdict columns have excessive unused width, while both descriptive columns are cramped and wrap heavily. The tall rows make comparisons harder.

raw.unsure: A, B and C differ only slightly in their descriptive column widths; their practical reading experience is very similar. E is a reasonable alternative if a more compact table matters more than keeping option names on one line.

r1B.why: Option names stay on one line, and the two descriptive columns have a balanced, readable rhythm. Weaknesses wraps a little more heavily than strengths.

ref_auto.why: The extra width for weaknesses improves its wrapping, but splitting two option names makes the first column harder to scan.

r3B.why: All option names stay intact, and weaknesses gets slightly more room than strengths. The paired descriptions and compact verdict column form a clear hierarchy.

contrast.why: Strengths has comfortable line lengths, but the narrow option column splits two names while weaknesses still wraps heavily.

ref_equal.why: The broad verdict column leaves substantial empty space while both descriptive columns become narrow and heavily wrapped, making rows tall and comparisons harder.

r1A.why: Option names remain intact and the descriptive columns are well balanced, though weaknesses wraps slightly more than in C.

raw.unsure: C and F are very close; the small difference in their descriptive-column widths produces only a modest change in wrapping.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
